## What This Code Does

This demo creates a cohort of agents using the model's `Person` class and analyses their initial attribute distributions. It validates that agents exhibit realistic variation (not all identical), values are properly clamped to valid ranges, and different configuration settings produce expected distribution shapes.

## Helper Classes

::: {#mock .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
class MockGrid:
    def get_neighbors(self, pos, include_center=False):
        return []

class MockModel:
    def __init__(self, seed=None):
        self.seed = seed
        self.grid = MockGrid()
        self.agents = []
        self.rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    def register_agent(self, agent):
        self.agents.append(agent)
```
:::


## Generate Agents

::: {#generate .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
config = {
    "initial_resilience_mean": 0.6, "initial_resilience_sd": 0.15,
    "initial_affect_mean": 0.1, "initial_affect_sd": 0.25,
    "initial_resources_mean": 0.7, "initial_resources_sd": 0.12,
    "stress_probability": 0.4, "coping_success_rate": 0.5, "subevents_per_day": 3,
}

agents = []
for i in range(100):
    model = MockModel(seed=1000 + i)
    agent = Person(model, config)
    agents.append(agent)
print(f"Generated {len(agents)} agents")
```

## Distribution Analysis

::: {#cell-distributions .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
resilience = [a.resilience for a in agents]
affect = [a.affect for a in agents]
resources = [a.resources for a in agents]
pss10 = [a.pss10 for a in agents]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(10, 8))
axes[0, 0].hist(resilience, bins=20, alpha=0.7, color="#3498db")
axes[0, 0].set_title(f"Resilience (mean={np.mean(resilience):.3f})")
axes[0, 1].hist(affect, bins=20, alpha=0.7, color="#e74c3c")
axes[0, 1].set_title(f"Affect (mean={np.mean(affect):.3f})")
axes[1, 0].hist(resources, bins=20, alpha=0.7, color="#2ecc71")
axes[1, 0].set_title(f"Resources (mean={np.mean(resources):.3f})")
axes[1, 1].hist(pss10, bins=20, alpha=0.7, color="#f39c12")
axes[1, 1].set_title(f"PSS-10 (mean={np.mean(pss10):.3f})")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Bounds and Variation Checks

::: {#bounds .cell execution_count=5}
``` {.python .cell-code}
all_res_ok = all(0 <= a.resilience <= 1 for a in agents)
all_aff_ok = all(-1 <= a.affect <= 1 for a in agents)
all_resrc_ok = all(0 <= a.resources <= 1 for a in agents)
print(f"Resilience [0,1]: {all_res_ok}")
print(f"Affect [-1,1]: {all_aff_ok}")
print(f"Resources [0,1]: {all_resrc_ok}")

unique_res = len(set(np.round(resilience, 4)))
unique_aff = len(set(np.round(affect, 4)))
print(f"Unique resilience values: {unique_res} / {len(agents)}")
print(f"Unique affect values: {unique_aff} / {len(agents)}")
```

## Why This Matters for the Simulation

Agent initialization is the foundation of every simulation run. Realistic variation at start ensures emergent population dynamics are meaningful rather than artefacts of identical starting conditions. Bounds enforcement guarantees that all downstream phases receive valid inputs, preventing numerical drift or NaN propagation.
